login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag lack of JWT claims or inability to locally validate as a bug when the request omitted resource.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs retain previously granted scopes until they expire, even after permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: A valid I3 test must obtain a new token after the change; old-token continued access until exp is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted permissions may not appear through refresh; a new authorization flow may be required.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat absence of newly granted scopes on refresh as a bug unless they were already requested in the original flow.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep their old scopes until expiration after permission changes; only newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag unchanged scopes in an already-issued JWT as stale-cache vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: If organization_id is omitted, only global roles and permissions are evaluated; organization RBAC is not enforced.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-org authorization tests must include organization_id or they are not exercising organization-scoped policy.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session/global sign-out clears the centralized session but does not revoke grants with offline_access by default.
oidc_jwt.note: Use explicit token revocation for revocation tests; surviving refresh capability after logout is documented behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Ending the centralized Logto session does not necessarily revoke grants associated with offline_access; refresh capability may persist until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat post-logout refresh success as a vulnerability unless explicit revocation was expected and tested.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing users signing in with enterprise SSO are automatically linked to an existing Logto account when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merging on matching email for enterprise SSO is by design and should not be flagged as an unexpected collision.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified in the authorization or token request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat non-JWT access tokens as missing claims or broken JWT validation. Use introspection or /oidc/me semantics instead.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct_sign_in fails because the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: A redirect to the normal sign-in page is expected fallback behavior, not flow confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT access tokens are stateless bearer tokens; documentation does not describe jti replay tracking for normal JWT bearer use, and Logto examples focus on signature/issuer/audience/expiration validation.
oidc_jwt.source: authorization/validate-access-tokens/*; RFC-aligned behavior reflected in docs
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing the same JWT access token is not by itself evidence of a replay vulnerability for standard bearer-token validation.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Logto issues opaque access tokens when no resource is specified in the authorization or token request. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT validation semantics, the fuzzer MUST include a resource parameter (or rely on a configured default API resource) so the returned access token is a JWT rather than an opaque token.

Default API resource behavior changes token format: if resource is omitted and no default API resource applies, Logto may issue an opaque token; if openid is included without resource, the access token for userinfo is opaque. JWT-focused tests MUST explicitly request the target API resource to avoid false positives caused by opaque-token behavior.

The resource parameter is exact-match only. Documentation states it must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). For I5 audience tests, do not use prefixes, shortened values, or wildcard-like patterns; they will not match a registered API resource.

Scope names are exact-match only. Documentation states permission names must exactly match the defined API permission names; prefixes and shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For I5 tests, request the full permission string and do not assume partial matches.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL token request using a valid token alongside the attack token. A failed protected-call result without a valid control cannot distinguish token-validation failure from broken API setup or missing permissions.

Audience validation is not automatically enforced in several Logto validation examples (verify_aud=false or manual audience checks). For I5 audience_mismatch and cross-provider audience tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure the target API under test explicitly validates aud against the expected resource indicator; otherwise acceptance is by application misconfiguration, not necessarily broker failure.

Issuer validation must use the exact issuer value from OIDC discovery or https://<tenant>/oidc. Since Logto does not allow customizing issuer or JWKS URI, I1 issuer tests MUST compare against that exact discovered issuer string; forged issuer values should be rejected.

JWKS trust anchor is fixed to the tenant JWKS endpoint (/oidc/jwks or discovery jwks_uri). For I1 trust-anchor-substitution and resign_attacker_key tests, the verifier MUST fetch keys only from the tenant JWKS and reject attacker-controlled keys or kid values not present in that JWKS.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization-scoped JWT behavior, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token (or use client_credentials) and then request the organization token with organization parameters. Do not expect an organization JWT directly from the initial code exchange.

Organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. For I5 organization-bound authorization tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id in the token request; otherwise the test is exercising global authorization, not organization authorization.

For organization-level API resource tests, the token request MUST include both resource and organization_id. Omitting organization_id disables organization RBAC; omitting resource changes the token type/target. Both are required to test organization-scoped JWT authorization correctly.

Permission changes do not mutate existing JWTs. Newly issued tokens reflect reduced scopes immediately, but existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. For I3 config-change or permission-tightening tests, the fuzzer MUST obtain a NEW token after the change and MUST NOT expect an already-issued JWT to shrink in place.

Global enlarged permissions do not appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set; a new authorization flow may be required. For I3/I5 permission-enlargement tests, do not treat missing newly granted scopes on refresh as a security bug unless the scopes were already within the original request set.

An access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. For I5 scope-escalation tests, the fuzzer must distinguish between broker over-granting within the requested set and legitimate omission of scopes never requested originally.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 token_exchange tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled; otherwise failures are expected configuration errors, not security rejections.

PAT-based token exchange and impersonation token exchange both use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange. For I5 token-exchange tests, the fuzzer MUST set subject_token_type exactly to the documented token type for the subject token being used; wrong token-type values cause setup failure rather than a meaningful security result.

Opaque token introspection requires client authentication using either HTTP Basic auth or client_id/client_secret in the POST body. Introspection failures without valid client auth are expected and must not be interpreted as token invalidity.

Current Logto SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out: it clears the centralized Logto session via the end-session flow. However, grants with offline_access are not revoked by end-session and may remain valid until grant TTL expiry. For I2/session revocation tests, do not assume browser sign-out revokes refresh-token-backed grants.

Grant TTL default is 180 days, and offline_access grants can survive end-session logout. For freshness/revocation tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly call token revocation when testing token invalidation; relying on browser logout alone can produce false positives because refresh-capable grants remain valid by design.

Logto supports PKCE and the token endpoint expects application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. For authorization-code tests, exchange_code_for_token MUST send code_verifier in form encoding; malformed content type or missing verifier causes protocol failure unrelated to the security invariant.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti on oidc_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT access token as a vulnerability by itself. Logto documents JWT access tokens as self-contained bearer tokens and opaque tokens as introspected tokens; there is no documentation of jti replay tracking for ordinary JWT bearer use. Replay resistance must instead be tested via exp/nbf/lifetime enforcement or token exchange semantics, not same-token reuse.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL token flow alongside the ATTACK flow. Logto documentation requires validating expiration and issuer, but many sample validators disable audience verification manually. Without a control token that is otherwise valid, a rejection may reflect broken test setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I1/I5 audience-binding tests against Logto-issued JWTs, the fuzzer MUST request a token with an explicit resource parameter whenever testing JWT access tokens. Logto issues opaque access tokens when no resource is specified; opaque tokens are intended for /oidc/me and require introspection, so JWT audience-validation tests are invalid unless resource is present or a default API resource is configured.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, resource matching is exact. Logto states the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator URI), and scope names must exactly match defined permission names. Do NOT use prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like values; they are not pattern matches.

For I5 scope/permission tests, requested scopes are exact string matches only. Logto explicitly states scope names must exactly match permission names and prefixes/shortened versions do not work as wildcards. For multi-permission scenarios, request each concrete scope explicitly; do not assume partial names or '*' semantics.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs are BY DESIGN immutable until expiry. Logto documents that permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid I3 test must compare NEW token issuance before and after the config change, not continued acceptance of an old token.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, a refresh token flow alone may not surface newly granted scopes unless those scopes were part of the original authorization request. Logto enforces a scope subset rule: newly issued tokens can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth flow. To test permission enlargement correctly, the original authorization request must already include the candidate scopes, or the client must run a new authorization flow.

For I3 organization-permission and organization-level API tests, organization context is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions. Do NOT interpret acceptance without organization_id as an organization-isolation failure.

For I5 organization token tests, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. You must first obtain a refresh token (or use client_credentials), then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token or client_credentials plus organization parameters. Testing organization JWT issuance directly from the code exchange will produce false negatives.

For I5 organization-level API tests, request both resource and organization_id together. Logto only includes both API audience and organization context in the JWT when both are supplied; omitting organization_id falls back to global RBAC, and omitting resource changes token type/semantics.

For I1/I5 token exchange tests, the target application must have token exchange explicitly enabled. Logto documents token exchange as disabled by default; if not enabled, /oidc/token returns an application-policy error rather than a security decision about subject_token, audience, or scope binding.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare exchanged scopes against both the requested scope and the original authorization context. Logto documents PAT-exchanged tokens as equivalent to refresh-token-derived tokens and enforces the same authorization model; scope expansion beyond upstream authorization should be tested on the exchanged token contents, not assumed from a 200 response alone.

For I1 cross-provider_jwt_audience and trust-anchor style tests involving external OIDC/enterprise SSO, use the authorization endpoint with direct_sign_in or normal OIDC browser flow, not /oidc/token as a raw JWT login endpoint. The provided Logto documentation does not describe any direct 'login_with_jwt' API for upstream JWT submission; Logto acts as OIDC provider at /oidc/* and upstream IdP validation occurs inside browser-based sign-in flows.

For I3 sign-out and session-coherence tests, distinguish local app sign-out from centralized Logto session termination. Logto documents client-side-only sign-out and end-session as separate layers. A test that only clears local tokens does not prove centralized session revocation failure.

For I2/I3 logout-related tests with offline_access, end-session does not necessarily revoke the app grant. Logto documents that if offline_access was granted, the grant may remain valid until grant TTL expiry even after centralized session end. Do NOT flag surviving refresh capability after logout as a bug unless the test specifically targets explicit revocation or documented grant semantics.

For I3 reauthentication tests, prompt=login forces credential entry and bypasses SSO. If the goal is to test silent session reuse or stale centralized session behavior, do NOT include prompt=login. Conversely, if the goal is to force fresh authentication, include prompt=login (and consent when offline_access is requested).

For OIDC request parameter tests, start_oidc_auth returns redirects and must not be auto-followed by the executor. Logto's authorization endpoint is redirect-driven; following redirects automatically can collapse distinct flow steps and hide state, direct_sign_in, or request-object handling issues.

The resource parameter uses EXACT string matching only. The requested resource MUST exactly match the registered API identifier URI; prefixes, shortened values, or wildcard-like values are not supported. For multi-resource or cross-provider tests, do not use patterns such as '*' or partial URIs.

Scope names use EXACT string matching only. Requested scopes must exactly match permission names defined in Logto; shortened names or wildcard-like values do not match. For I5 tests, do not assume prefix matching or wildcard expansion for scopes.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL flow that requests a valid JWT access token for the same resource and succeeds. Without a resource parameter, Logto may issue an opaque token instead, making JWT-claim freshness tests invalid or misinterpreted.

If organization_id is omitted when requesting a token for an organization-level API, Logto evaluates only global roles/permissions and does not apply organization RBAC. I5 organization-binding tests MUST include organization_id in the token request.

For organization-level API tokens, the token request MUST include both resource and organization_id. Omitting resource changes the token type/target, and omitting organization_id disables organization RBAC evaluation.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled in application settings, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

For PAT-based or impersonation-style token exchange, /oidc/token accepts either HTTP Basic client authentication or body client_id for public clients. The fuzzer MUST use the authentication mode appropriate to the application type; otherwise token exchange failures are expected setup errors.

Permission changes do not mutate existing JWTs. Newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions immediately, but existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. Valid I3 permission-change tests MUST compare a pre-change token with a newly issued post-change token, not expect an already-issued JWT to change in place.

For enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh does NOT add scopes that were not part of the original authorization request. The client must run a new authorization flow to obtain newly granted scopes outside the original request set. Do not treat missing newly granted scopes after refresh as a bug.

OIDC discovery is available at /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration and the issuer is fixed to the tenant OIDC URL; Logto does not support customizing issuer or JWKS URI independently. I1 issuer/JWKS validation tests must use the discovered issuer and jwks_uri as the trust anchor baseline.

Logto's userinfo endpoint is mounted at /oidc/me, not /userinfo. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/me for verify_granted_identity; using a generic /userinfo path will produce false negatives unrelated to security behavior.

Current SDK sign-out behavior is effectively global sign-out: it redirects to /session/end and auto-confirms logout. However, if offline_access was granted, end-session does not revoke that app grant by default. I2/I3 logout tests MUST distinguish cleared browser session from surviving refresh-token grant state.

Default grant TTL is 180 days, and grants with offline_access can survive end-session until grant expiry unless explicitly revoked. Do not interpret successful token refresh after browser logout as proof of logout bypass when offline_access was granted; this is documented behavior.

For high-assurance reauthentication tests, use prompt=login (and prompt=login consent when offline_access is requested). Without prompt=login, an existing Logto session may silently satisfy authentication and invalidate I3 flow assumptions about fresh user interaction.

Direct sign-in is still initiated through /oidc/auth with the direct_sign_in parameter; it is not an API login bypass. If the connector is missing or disabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page. Tests must not treat fallback-to-login-page as evidence of connector confusion or auth bypass.

For OIDC request-object tests, start_oidc_auth supports the request parameter as a JWT request object. Because Logto documents standard OIDC auth parameters and request forwarding through /oidc/auth, alg=none or tampered request-object tests must be executed at the authorization endpoint, not the token endpoint.
oidc_jwt.source: end-user-flows/authentication-parameters/README.mdx; task rule for standard OIDC endpoints

oidc_jwt.constraint: When validating Logto-issued JWTs, many example integrations disable automatic audience verification in the JWT library and require manual audience checks based on permission model. I5 tests against relying APIs MUST explicitly verify aud against the registered API resource indicator and, for organization APIs, also verify organization context.

For organization permission tokens, validate both permissions and context: organization_id claim and appropriate audience semantics. A token with correct scopes but wrong or missing organization context is not valid for organization-scoped authorization tests.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
